example: I can't come to school today because I feel under the weather.
origin: Possibly from sailors who felt sick when the ship moved in rough weather at sea

wrong_meanings.meaning: to stand outside in bad weather
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This takes the words literally. The idiom describes how a person feels, not where they are standing.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to feel very happy and relaxed
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the real meaning. Feeling well is not what the idiom expresses.
The idiom has nothing to do with fear. It describes a mild illness.

explanation: 'Under the weather' means feeling slightly sick or not quite well. It is a common, informal way to talk about a mild illness.
